title: Complaint under Consumer Protection Act, 2019
description: Definition of Complaint as per the Consumer Protection Act, 2019

content.legal_definition: any allegation in writing, made by a complainant for obtaining any relief provided by or under this Act, that— (i) an unfair contract or unfair trade practice or a restrictive trade practice has been adopted by any trader or service provider; (ii) the goods bought by him or agreed to be bought by him suffer from one or more defects; (iii) the services hired or availed of or agreed to be hired or availed of by him suffer from any deficiency; (iv) a trader or a service provider, as the case may be, has charged for the goods or for the services mentioned in the complaint, a price in excess of the price— (a) fixed by or under any law for the time being in force; or (b) displayed on the goods or any package containing such goods; or (c) displayed on the price list exhibited by him by or under any law for the time being in force; or (d) agreed between the parties; (v) the goods, which are hazardous to life and safety when used, are being offered for sale to the public— (a) in contravention of standards relating to safety of such goods as required to be complied with, by or under any law for the time being in force; (b) where the trader knows that the goods so offered are unsafe to the public; (vi) the services which are hazardous or likely to be hazardous to life and safety of the public when used, are being offered by a person who provides any service and who knows it to be injurious to life and safety; (vii) a claim for product liability action lies against the product manufacturer, product seller or product service provider, as the case may be;
content.plain_language: A complaint is a written allegation made by a complainant to get relief under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, claiming that a trader or service provider has engaged in an unfair contract, unfair trade practice or restrictive trade practice, sold defective goods, provided deficient services, overcharged, sold hazardous goods, offered hazardous services, or that a product liability action lies against the product manufacturer, product seller or product service provider.
examples: A consumer buys a defective phone and files a complaint against the seller.
A person hires a service provider who fails to deliver the promised services and files a complaint.
non_examples: A consumer verbally tells a friend about a bad experience with a product.
A person writes a positive review about a product.

title: Consumer
description: Definition of Consumer

content.legal_definition: "consumer" means any person who— (i) buys any goods for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment and includes any user of such goods other than the person who buys such goods for consideration paid or promised or partly paid or partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, when such use is made with the approval of such person, but does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose; or (ii) hires or avails of any services for a consideration which has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment and includes any beneficiary of such service other than the person who hires or avails of the services for consideration paid or promised, or partly paid and partly promised, or under any system of deferred payment, when such services are availed of with the approval of the first mentioned person, but does not include a person who avails of such service for any commercial purpose.
content.plain_language: A consumer is a person who buys goods or hires services for a consideration which is paid, promised, partly paid and partly promised, or under a deferred payment system, and includes any user of such goods or beneficiary of such services when the use is made with the approval of the buyer or the person hiring the services. It does not include a person who obtains goods for resale or for any commercial purpose, or who avails of services for any commercial purpose.
examples: A person who buys a laptop for personal use
A person who hires a plumber to fix their home
A family member who uses a refrigerator bought by another person, with the buyer's approval, is also a consumer
A person who receives services hired by someone else, with the first person's approval, is also a consumer
non_examples: A person who buys goods to resell them
A person who uses a service for a commercial purpose
A person who uses goods bought by another without the buyer's approval

title: Consumer Rights

content.legal_definition: the right to be protected against the marketing of goods, products or services which are hazardous to life and property; the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price of goods, products or services, as the case may be, so as to protect the consumer against unfair trade practices; the right to be assured, wherever possible, access to a variety of goods, products or services at competitive prices; the right to be heard and to be assured that consumer's interests will receive due consideration at appropriate fora; the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practice or restrictive trade practices or unscrupulous exploitation of consumers; and the right to consumer awareness
content.plain_language: The rights that protect consumers from hazardous or unfair products and services, ensure access to accurate information, access to a variety of goods at competitive prices, the right to be heard, the right to seek redressal against unfair or restrictive trade practices, and the right to consumer awareness
examples: A consumer's right to know the ingredients in a food product to avoid allergic reactions
A consumer's right to file a complaint against a company for selling defective products

A consumer's right to seek redressal against an unfair trade practice, restrictive trade practice or unscrupulous exploitation
non_examples: A business's internal procedures that keep consumers from filing complaints
The right to be heard is not a guarantee that the complaint will succeed: winning depends on the merits examined by the forum (interpretive note)
The right to seek redressal is not itself a guarantee that a refund, replacement or compensation will be ordered (interpretive note)

content.plain_language: a business practice that unfairly controls prices, delivery, or supply of goods and services, causing unnecessary costs or limitations for consumers. examples: A company delays shipping products to create a shortage and increase prices.

A retailer requires customers to buy a related product to purchase a desired item, such as requiring an extended warranty purchase as a condition for buying a washing machine; this condition-precedent requirement is itself covered by clause (ii) of section 2(41)

A retailer says the consumer can buy a laptop only if they also purchase a Rs. 5000 antivirus package; the condition-precedent requirement falls within clause (ii) of section 2(41) without separate proof of price or supply manipulation

description: Definition of Unfair Contract under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019

content.legal_definition: a contract between a manufacturer or trader or service provider on one hand, and a consumer on the other, having such terms which cause significant change in the rights of such consumer, including the following, namely:— (i) requiring manifestly excessive security deposits to be given by a consumer for the performance of contractual obligations; or (ii) imposing any penalty on the consumer, for the breach of contract thereof which is wholly disproportionate to the loss occurred due to such breach to the other party to the contract; or (iii) refusing to accept early repayment of debts on payment of applicable penalty; or (iv) entitling a party to the contract to terminate such contract unilaterally, without reasonable cause; or (v) permitting or has the effect of permitting one party to assign the contract to the detriment of the other party who is a consumer, without his consent; or (vi) imposing on the consumer any unreasonable charge, obligation or condition which puts such consumer to disadvantage
content.plain_language: a contract between a manufacturer, trader or service provider and a consumer having terms that cause a significant change in the consumer's rights, including requiring manifestly excessive security deposits, imposing penalties disproportionate to the loss, refusing to accept early repayment of debts on payment of applicable penalty, allowing unilateral termination without reasonable cause, permitting assignment of the contract to the consumer's detriment without consent, or imposing unreasonable charges, obligations or conditions on the consumer
examples: a contract that requires a consumer to pay a security deposit that is much higher than the value of the service provided
a contract that imposes a penalty on a consumer for breaching the contract that is much higher than the actual loss suffered by the other party
non_examples: a contract that requires a reasonable security deposit for a service
a contract that imposes a penalty on a consumer for breaching the contract that is proportionate to the actual loss suffered by the other party

title: Unfair Trade Practice
description: Definition of Unfair Trade Practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019

content.legal_definition: a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice including any of the following practices
content.plain_language: a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice, including false advertising, hiding information or making false promises
examples: a company advertising a product as 'new' when it's actually refurbished
a business making false claims about the quality of their services
non_examples: a company offering a genuine discount on a product
a business providing clear and accurate information about their services
